h1: The 7 Best Compact Printers for Small Desks of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven compact printers for small desks, from Canon and HP inkjets to a Brother laser and a pocket thermal model.
summary: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 is the best all-round compact printer, with duplex printing in a small body. Choose the TS6520 if you want an on-printer display, the TR4720 for scanning multi-page documents, and the Brother HL-L2405W if you mostly print text. The thermal MT610Pro suits desks with almost no room.
intro: A desk-friendly printer is one you can forget about between jobs, and the footprint printed on the box rarely tells you that. Ink that dries out, a paper tray that sticks out, or a scanner lid you cannot open under a shelf can turn a small printer into a daily annoyance.

We ranked seven compact models on paper, weighing body size, what each can do, how ink or toner behaves when idle, and the limits buried in spec lines. Rankings come from the spec sheet and owner reports, not bench measurements.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small color all-in-one that still prints on both sides of the page.
products.description:
The TS4320 is a compact color inkjet that prints, copies and scans, and it adds automatic two-sided printing. It connects over wireless and works with the Canon PRINT mobile app.

It ranks first because duplex printing is rare at this size and keeps paper stacks thin on a small desk. Against the TS6520 below, you give up the built-in OLED screen, which is a minor loss for most home users.

Buy it if you want one tidy machine for school and home paperwork. The caveat is that it handles only letter and A4 paper, with no legal or tabloid sizes.
products.idealFor: Students and remote workers needing a complete small printer.
products.skipIf: You print mostly black text and want toner.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Same compact all-in-one idea, with a small screen for status checks.
products.description:
The TS6520 is a compact color inkjet all-in-one with a 1.42 inch OLED display and automatic duplex printing. Setup runs through the Canon PRINT app.

It lands just behind the TS4320 because the screen is a convenience, not a capability, and both share the same feature set otherwise. The display does let you check ink or errors without reaching for a phone.

Pick it if you like seeing status on the machine itself. The caveat is the cost of that screen: it sits in the same $50-100 bucket, so choose it only if you will actually use the display.
products.idealFor: Households who want status shown on the printer.
products.skipIf: You are happy managing everything from a phone.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: The only pick here with an automatic document feeder and fax.
products.description:
The TR4720 is a compact all-in-one that adds an auto document feeder and built-in fax to the usual print and scan duties. It pairs with mobile printing through the Canon PRINT app.

It sits third because the feeder adds bulk to a small desk, and the listing does not mention duplex printing. The tradeoff versus the TS4320 is paper handling for document handling.

It is a strong choice for people who scan multi-page forms or still send faxes. The caveat is that feeder body, so measure your shelf before ordering.
products.idealFor: Home offices that scan or fax multi-page documents.
products.skipIf: You rarely scan and want the smallest body.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact HP all-in-one that leans on an ink subscription trial.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 is a compact color inkjet that prints, scans and copies, pairs through the HP Smart app and includes a three-month HP Instant Ink trial. It also lists AI-assisted print management features.

It ranks fourth because its appeal depends on the ink trial, and subscription ink can feel limiting once the trial ends. The Canon models list duplex printing; this listing does not.

Choose it if you already use the HP app and want a gentle start on ink. The caveat is that you should read the Instant Ink terms before relying on the plan.
products.idealFor: New printer owners wanting a gentle start on ink costs.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS3720 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: The no-frills option for occasional printing in a tiny footprint.
products.description:
The TS3720 is a basic compact color all-in-one that prints, copies and scans, with wireless setup through the Canon PRINT app. It has a small, no-frills body.

It ranks fifth because it lacks automatic duplex printing, which the TS4320 and TS6520 include. That is the main reason to step up a model within the $50-100 bucket.

Best for people who print a few pages a month. The caveat is manual two-sided printing, which takes extra steps and wastes time on bigger jobs.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A print-only laser whose toner will not dry out on you.
products.description:
The HL-L2405W is a compact monochrome laser that prints only, with wireless mobile printing and Alexa compatibility. The listing notes that toner does not dry out between uses.

It ranks sixth purely because it cannot scan or copy and prints in black only, which is a bigger limit than the Canon all-in-ones. The tradeoff is reliability when the printer sits idle for weeks.

Choose it if you print mainly text and want a machine that works when you need it. The caveat is the lack of scan and copy, which means a second device for any scanning.
products.idealFor: Text-heavy printing with long gaps between jobs.
products.skipIf: You need color or a scanner.

products.name: Inkless Portable Bluetooth Thermal Printer (MT610Pro)
products.verdict: Pocket-sized inkless printing for desks with no room for anything else.
products.description:
The MT610Pro is an inkless Bluetooth thermal printer at 300 DPI that handles 8.5 x 11 inch Letter and A4 paper. It pairs with iOS, Android and laptops, and it is the smallest, lightest device in this list.

It ranks last because it needs special thermal paper rather than standard copy paper, which adds a running cost and a supply to remember. That limit separates it from every other pick here.

Buy it for occasional printing where space is the only concern. The caveat is that thermal output is not meant for color work.
products.idealFor: Occasional printing where desk space is minimal.

whatMatters.detail: Inkjet, laser and thermal printers behave very differently. Inkjets handle color and photos but ink can dry out; lasers print sharp text and keep toner for months; thermal prints without ink but needs special paper. Check the listing title for the type, since it decides running costs.

Duplex means the printer flips the sheet itself to print on both sides. It halves paper use and keeps stacks thin on a cramped desk. Look for the words auto duplex in the spec bullets; the TS4320 and TS6520 list it, while the TS3720 does not.

Not every compact printer scans. The Brother HL-L2405W is print only, while the Canon all-in-ones scan and copy. If you scan multi-page paperwork, look for an automatic document feeder, as on the TR4720, rather than a flatbed alone.

Most compact printers accept letter and A4 only. If you print legal documents or large posters, this matters. Check the listing for supported sizes and be wary of silence, since it usually means standard letter.

Inkjet cartridges can dry if the printer sits unused, leading to clogged heads. Laser toner does not dry out, as noted for the Brother. If you print rarely, a laser or thermal model may avoid wasted cartridges.

howToChoose.intro: How often and what you print decides the technology.

rows: Mostly black text, long idle gaps

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Prints in color and handles photos, but cartridges can dry out when idle. The Canon TS4320, TS6520, TS3720, TR4720 and HP DeskJet 4355 are inkjets.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Monochrome laser prints sharp text, and toner does not dry out between uses. The Brother HL-L2405W is the laser pick.

howToChoose.note: Most home users should default to inkjet unless they print only black text.

rows: Room for a bit more body

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Wireless setup, automatic duplex to save paper, and a scanner for contracts and forms.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 covers all three, and the TR4720 adds a document feeder for longer scans.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print rarely and hate dried ink, which points to the Brother HL-L2405W, or you scan stacks of pages, which points to the TR4720.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print a few pages monthly. The Canon TS3720 does the basics.

faq.q: Will these printers fit under a shelf?
faq.a: Check the listing for exact dimensions, since scanner lids and paper trays need extra clearance. The thermal MT610Pro is the easiest to store.

faq.q: Do I need special paper for the thermal printer?
faq.a: Yes. The MT610Pro requires thermal paper, not standard copy paper, so plan for that running cost.

faq.q: Is the Brother laser worth it over a Canon inkjet?
faq.a: Only if you print mostly black text and rarely use it. Toner does not dry out, but you lose color, scanning and copying.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying a small printer?
faq.a: Ignoring paper size limits. These Canon models are letter and A4 only, so legal documents will not work.

faq.q: How do I set up the Canon models?
faq.a: Install the Canon PRINT app on your phone, then follow the wireless setup prompts. It works with iOS and Android.

faq.q: What happens to the HP Instant Ink trial?
faq.a: The three-month trial ends, after which you decide whether to subscribe. Read the terms first so you know the ongoing plan.

finalTake: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 is the sensible default for a small desk, with duplex and scanning in a compact body. Step up to the TR4720 if scanning stacks matter, or to the Brother if you print text sporadically. Reserve the thermal MT610Pro for desks with truly no room.
